newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip sales.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close low on blue chip sales.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower for a second straight day as retailers took profits among highly capitalised blue chips, brokers said.
The all share index closed 5.0 points down at 816.7 with price declines outnumbering gains by 52 to 19. Aitken Spence fell 9.75 rupees to 195, Commercial Bank six to 225.
"There is a lot of profit to take among most stocks, but selling of highly capitalised blue chips has the most impact on the index," said Subram Ramaswamy of Bartleet Mallory Stock brokers.
Turnover was 54.5 million rupees. Foreign buying was worth 26.8 million rupees and selling was 10.2 million.
Colombo stocks which began a correction on Tuesday after rising 37 points in five days, are not expected to fall far below 810 points, brokers said.
"There are buyers already straining at the leash to come in, the only thing holding them back is the lack of quantities at lower prices," said one.
The government, meanwhile, postponed the sale of a strategic holding in Elkaduwa Plantations Ltd, which was to take place on the stock exchange on Wednesday.
Elkaduwa was one of four estate firms where the government was selling 51 percent or 10.2 million shares to a strategic investor, as part of its plantation sector reform programme.
